label: complementary
rationale: The predicate `arrested` describes a state of being detained, typically by a law enforcement entity, while the predicate `has` describes possession of an item. These predicates represent fundamentally different concepts. `arrested` relates to legal status, whereas `has` relates to ownership. The action contexts further illustrate this difference: `arrested` involves a coercive action, while `has` describes a voluntary relationship. The `arrest_meteor` action explicitly involves detaining an entity, while the `buy_boots` action involves acquiring an item. Therefore, they are complementary – they describe distinct relationships between entities and items, but they are not interchangeable. The use of `entity` as a type parameter in both predicates reinforces this distinction.
